info.title: bank8-fdx
info.description: Sentin8 Bank8:FDX - open banking, FDX v6.5 provider/recipient.

get.summary:
`GET /fdx/consents/callback` - OAuth callback from Auth after consent.
Per the FDX design §4.3:
5. External provider redirects to Auth callback
6. Auth validates state, nonce, JARM
7. Auth exchanges code for tokens
8. FDX creates consent record (active), enqueues data retrieval
For now (dev), this activates the consent and redirects back to the
eFintech app. In production, this would exchange the code for tokens
at Auth, store the token grants, and enqueue data retrieval.

`GET /fdx/v6/accounts` - search customer accounts (proxies to Ledger).
The incoming Bearer (the bank's own customer token OR a delegated
recipient token - both carry the provider customer as `sub`) is
forwarded to Ledger, so RLS scopes the rows to the consenting
customer either way (fdx DESIGN.md §1 - the consent grant keys on the
token subject).

`GET /fdx/v6/accounts/{accountId}/payment-networks/{paymentNetworkId}`
the payment network(s) for this `bankId`/`identifier` pair (; proxy
to Ledger's payment-networks read, filtered to the requested id).

`GET /fdx/v6/accounts/{accountId}/payment-networks/{paymentNetworkId}/revocation`
- revocation lifecycle events for the identifier.

put.summary:
`PUT /fdx/v6/accounts/{accountId}/payment-networks/{paymentNetworkId}/revocation`
- revoke the payment network identifier (; persists the revocation
record and answers 204 No Content per spec).

get.summary:
`GET /fdx/v6/accounts/{accountId}/statements/{statementId}` - statement
download. The Ledger statement object lives in Sentin8:Storage at
`buckets/statements/objects/{envId}/{accountId}/{statementId}.pdf`;
this handler mints a short-lived read URL via the Storage link API and
answers 302 Found with the `Location` header (spec: statement image may
be served inline or via redirect; §5.0a signed URLs).

302.description: Redirect to the signed statement URL (Storage link API)

get.summary:
`GET /fdx/v6/accounts/{accountId}/transactions` - transactions (proxies
to Ledger; no hardcoded empty results).

`GET /fdx/v6/certification-metrics` - certification metrics (design
§10: counts over the tables this service already owns - `data_call*`
rows in `audit_events` plus consent granted/revoked transitions -
behind a short bounded cache; the rollup table + evidence admin page
are the follow-on). The literal-zero stub is gone: these are real
counters now.

put.summary:
`PUT /fdx/v6/consents/{consentId}/revocation` - the FDX
RevocationRequest (reason/initiator/otherReason). Existing handler
`handlers::revoke_fdx_consent` is extended here: the revocation
row is persisted and a CONSENT_REVOKED notification is queued.

post.summary:
`POST /fdx/v6/consents/{consentId}/revoke` - POST alias of the PUT
revocation surface (fdx DESIGN.md §4): the recipient-side fdx instance
calls this with the delegated provider token after revoking its own
registry row, so a fintech-initiated revocation lands on the provider's
grant ledger and takes effect on the next data call. The delegated
token's `sub` IS the grant's customer - the same subject the bank's own
dashboard revokes for.

200.description: Revoked via the POST alias (delegates to the PUT revocation surface)

403.description: Delegated subject must be the grant's customer

post.summary:
`POST /fdx/v6/notification-subscriptions` - create a subscription
/. The per-subscription HMAC secret is generated here and
stored as a sentin8-secrets:// reference - never plaintext.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /fdx/v6/notification-subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` - delete a
subscription (; soft delete + release the secret reference).

get.summary:
`GET /fdx/v6/notifications` - notification feed (polling alternative to
webhook delivery; ).

post.summary:
`POST /fdx/v6/notifications` - inbound notification ingest (
`fdx:notifications:publish`). Records the notification, queues it for
delivery to matching subscriptions, and emits the Bus event the
delivery consumer reacts to.

get.summary:
`GET /fdx/v6/operation-support` - explicit machine-readable statement of
which FDX families this provider implements vs reserves (§3.1); pairs
with the middleware 501s so clients can preflight.

post.summary:
`POST /fdx/v6/payment-initiation-parties/{partyId}/payment-methods`
register a payment method for the party.

get.summary:
`GET /fdx/v6/recurring-payments` - search recurring payments (;
proxies the payments scheduled-payments list).

post.summary:
`POST /fdx/v6/recurring-payments` - create a recurring payment
(; backed by Bank8:Payments `scheduled_payments`).

get.summary:
`GET /fdx/v6/recurring-payments/{recurringPaymentId}/payments` - the
executed occurrences (; proxies payments for the source schedule).

delete.summary:
`DELETE /fdx/v6/transfers/{transferId}` - cancel a transfer (spec
`cancelTransfer`; proxies Bank8:Payments cancel where the scheme allows).

patch.summary:
`PATCH /fdx/v6/transfers/{transferId}` - update a transfer (amount/due
date where the scheme allows; proxies Bank8:Payments).

get.summary: GET /v1/admin/ui/{page} - return RFW definition for the requested admin page.

`GET /v1/auth/consent/accounts` - data endpoint for account selection.
Returns the customer's accounts at this Data Provider. Called by the
RFW page's data fetch (proxied by Sentin8:Auth with a short-lived JWT).
Fetches accounts from Bank8:Ledger.

`GET /v1/auth/consent/ui` - return RFW consent page definition.
Returns a JSON RFW definition that auth-ui renders. The definition
includes:
- Scope list with FDX-specific descriptions and Material Icons code points
- Account selection DataTable (checkboxes, nickname, type, masked number, balance)
- "Authorize" button (POST to /v1/auth/consent/approve)
- "Deny" button (POST to /v1/auth/consent/deny)
- Data endpoint declaration for account fetch (/v1/auth/consent/accounts)

post.summary: `POST /v1/internal/steps/execute` - Flow proxy-back for FDX domain steps.

get.summary:
`GET /v1/recipient/accounts` - list consented accounts for the recipient.
If `consent_id` is provided, returns only the accounts the customer
selected during the provider's consent screen (per FDX UX Guidelines
§3.1.6 "Select Accounts"). The account IDs are stored in
consent_resources and used to filter the Ledger account list.
If no consent_id is provided, returns all accounts (backward compat).

`GET /v1/recipient/consents` - list active consents for the recipient.
Returns `{"consents": [...]}` (wrapped) so the eFintech app's
FdxConsentsHook can parse `response.data['consents']`.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/recipient/consents/start` - start consent authorization.
The two-ledger recipient flow (fdx DESIGN.md §1 + §4 consent-flow
sequence): the recipient-side fdx instance writes its OWN registry
(a `pending` row in `recipient_consents`, in the recipient tenant),
ensures its per-provider OAuth client exists at the provider's
authorization server (DCR, cached in `fdx.recipients`), and pushes a
PAR request whose `state` carries `"<consent handle>|<app origin>"`.
The AS's authorize screen runs the ceremony; the browser redirect
comes back to THIS instance's `/fdx/consents/callback` (the
registered redirect_uri), which activates the row and exchanges the
code. The provider's grant row is seeded by the provider's OWN
auth-family consumer from `sentin8:auth:grant:created` - never by
this side.

get.summary:
`GET /v1/recipient/providers` - list FDX data providers from the
`provider_profiles` registry.
Provider profiles are auto-registered when an environment's
`is_fdx_provider` flag is turned on (see Sys `update_env`), with the
env's auth domain used as the issuer URL. The table has no RLS, so the
catalog is visible cross-org - any recipient can discover and connect to
any active provider. No static seed data is required.
Response shape matches the eFintech recipient catalog contract:
`{ "providers": [{ id, name, supportedDataClusters, status, ... }] }`,
where each card reads `name`, `supportedDataClusters`, and `status`.
`GET /v1/recipient/providers/{id}` - get a specific FDX data provider.

ConsentApproveRequest.description:
`POST /v1/auth/consent/approve` - process consent approval.
Receives form data from the RFW page (selected account IDs, consent
metadata). Persists consent resources and returns the redirect URL.

ConsentCallbackQuery.description:
Query params for `GET /fdx/consents/callback` - the OAuth callback after
the customer approves/denies consent at the provider's Auth.

app_redirect_uri.description: The app return URL (passed through from BFF as `app_redirect_uri`).

error.description: OAuth error if the customer denied.

selected_account_ids.description:
Comma-separated list of account IDs the customer selected to share
during the provider's consent screen (FDX UX Guidelines §3.1.6).
Passed through from Auth's authorize/continue as a query param on
the redirect_uri.

state.description: The consent_id (passed as OAuth `state` in the PAR request).

redirect_url.description: The URL to navigate back to (the auth flow continuation).

authorization_url.description: The provider authorization URL to open.

ContainerDirection.description: Layout direction for a container's children.

FdxAccountsPassthrough.description:
FDX account/customer/statement passthrough envelope (OAPEC-9 honest
freeform): the forwarded provider document (Ledger/Payments payload,
CSDF-minimized) is provider-controlled, so the response body IS the
forwarded document itself - serialized transparently (wire-identical),
documented as an open object to keep the schema non-empty without
inventing fields the ledger owns.
